newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan landslide buries homes in mud, kills 14.
newsitem.headline: Japan landslide buries homes in mud, kills 14.

text.p: A landslide that buried houses in mud up to their roofs killed at least 14 people and left about eight missing on Thursday in a devastated village on Japan's southern Kyushu island, police reported.
Triggered by several days of torrential rain, a wall of mud and rock swept over Harihara village shortly after midnight, giving sleeping residents little chance of escape.
"We now have 14 people confirmed dead and eight missing," a Kagoshima Prefectural Police spokesman told Reuters.
Fifteen more people were in nearby hospitals.
The landslide tumbled over the village in Kagoshima Prefecture, 985 km (615 miles) southwest of Tokyo, around 12.50 a.m. (1550 GMT) on Thursday.
It buried 15 homes with a total of 40 residents.
The village, which is home to 80 families, is located on the Harihara River near the seaside city of Izumi.
"It came all of a sudden. The ground roared loudly. There was no time to escape," a middle-aged woman said.

The landslide started on a small mountain overlooking the village. Mud and rocks tumbled down the side of the mountain, bursting through a barrier wall that was under construction to head off just such a disaster.
The tons of rock and mud poured into the narrow Harihara river, causing it to burst its banks and spread across the valley at the bottom of the mountain.
Rescuers speculated that some of the missing may have been washed several miles (kms) down the river into the ocean.
Japan's Meteorological Agency said the area had received 800 millimetres (32 inches) of rain in the past few days, one-third of the area's normal rainfall for an entire year.
Rain was still falling in the area and rescue attempts were halted because of fears of more landslides, the police spokesman said.
"The rain is making the operation difficult," he said.
Kagoshima Governor Tatsuro Suga asked for military help in handling the disaster.
The area is designated as landslide-prone and a barrier to prevent landslides was under construction and near completion about 100 meters (yards) away from the buried village.
Another landslide on Wednesday night in neighbouring Kumamoto Prefecture buried nine people under mud, but they were all rescued, the police spokesman said.
Last December, 20 people died in another landslide in Kagoshima Prefecture.
Live television broadcasts from the scene showed splintered wooden homes with their roofs barely poking through the mud and other debris.
"Our neighbour's house is gone and so is the one next to it. I was just shaking. I don't know why I am alive," said a woman who was being treated at a nearby hospital.
A man whose son-in-law was among the missing added, "I tried walking to the village when I heard about the disaster but the mud kept coming and I couldn't get near."
"We've never experienced a flood this bad before," he said.
